requirements.R01_WRITER_FENCING: Only one writable process may own a database directory and ownership must be released on exit; the lock primitive and diagnostic wording are not compatibility contracts.
requirements.R03_SNAPSHOT_POINT_READS: Transactions retain begin-time point-read visibility while exposing their own puts and deletes.
requirements.R04_PREFIX_SCAN_SEMANTICS: Prefix scans retain transaction snapshot visibility, local overlays, raw-byte prefix filtering and unsigned byte ordering.
requirements.R05_WRITE_CONFLICTS: First-committer-wins stale writes are rejected atomically, end the transaction and do not publish partial state.
requirements.R06_SEQUENCE_DURABILITY: Successful commits use contiguous durable sequences, return only after durable commit publication, and rejected conflicts do not consume a sequence.
requirements.R07_UNCOMMITTED_RECOVERY: Killed and rolled-back transactions remain invisible after restart.
requirements.R08_WAL_RECOVERY_INTEGRITY: Only in-range short final WAL tails are repairable; complete corruption, invalid framing/type/payload and invalid commit history fail closed while the published layout remains readable.
requirements.R09_CHECKPOINT_LIFECYCLE: Checkpoint requires quiescence, crash-safely publishes rows/sequence before WAL reclamation and reclaims wal.log to zero bytes on success.
requirements.R10_SNAPSHOT_INTEGRITY: Published snapshots preserve the documented layout/CRC and reject checksum, truncation, duplicate/order, size, row-count, magic and trailing-byte corruption while stale snapshot.tmp is discarded.
requirements.R11_STATS: STATS reports durable sequence, visible committed-key count and actual WAL byte size.
requirements.R12_HEALTH: HEALTH validates reachable catalog/transaction/durable-path invariants, reports exact healthy state and fails closed with ERR on a detected invariant violation.
requirements.R13_BINARY_HEX: Keys, values and prefixes support arbitrary binary bytes through case-insensitive hexadecimal input and lowercase output.
requirements.R14_INCLUSIVE_LIMITS: 4096-byte key/prefix and 1048576-byte value limits are inclusive and oversized inputs are rejected consistently without terminating the process.
requirements.R15_PROTOCOL_RESILIENCE: Malformed commands and unknown transaction IDs return ERR consistently across command families while the session remains usable.
requirements.R16_NATIVE_COMPATIBILITY: The product remains C++20 and Rust only, preserves exact documented public C ABI signatures/linkage, exact stable wire shapes and published WAL/snapshot compatibility.

C_INCLUSIVE_SIZE_BOUNDARY.rationale: Key, value, and scan-prefix probes exercise the same shared decoded-size boundary rule at three public protocol positions; they are independent probes of one behavioral case rather than three distinct requirements.

C_LOCAL_SCAN_OVERLAY.rationale: Both probes fail the starter because SCAN omits an uncommitted local put. The hexadecimal probe additionally exercises uppercase operands and lowercase rendering, but its starter-to-Oracle transition is caused by the same local-scan-overlay invariant; committed hexadecimal canonicalization is preserved independently.

negative_failure_coverage: malformed protocol and unknown transaction IDs across command families
independence: Runtime pytest probes use isolated databases. WAL and snapshot compatibility fixtures are encoded from the solver-visible format contract rather than product serializers. C ABI/C++20 preservation is compiler-validated against the published header and native sources.
classification_note: F2P/P2P remain private authoring classifications; neutral pytest names are intentional. Q4 remediation removed the mechanism-coupled lock probe and two weak preservation probes, then added 19 contract probes. Current empirical evidence confirms exactly 30 F2P probes fail the starter and all 33 P2P probes pass it; Oracle passes all 63 probes. Two explicit grouping rules reduce 30 probes to 27 distinct change-required behavioral cases.

empirical_evidence.f2p_transition: 30/30 classified F2P probes fail starter and pass Oracle
empirical_evidence.p2p_preservation: 33/33 classified P2P probes pass starter and Oracle
